about: The conditions users have: folder sizes, files, storage and session length. Read by every product's scale and performance tests; rules in docs/shared/USAGE_CONDITIONS.md. Validated by scripts/check_conditions_contract.py.

typical.use: the size a test of an everyday folder uses
typical.source: a phone camera roll holds 2,000-50,000 photos, a desk cull 500-3,000 per shoot, a shared cloud folder 100-2,000

pr.use: every scale test that runs on every pull request
pr.source: decided 2026-11-15 after F-TOK-098 (3-5 s freeze per swipe at 3,032 photos)

stress.use: the release stress run (release-product), never the PR gate
stress.source: the upper bound of a years-deep phone camera roll

growth_check.rule: a scale test times the same operation at N and at factor*N (N = pr/factor) and fails when time(factor*N)/time(N) exceeds max_ratio: linear work gives about 4, quadratic about 16. Absolute milliseconds are never asserted in the PR gate.

layouts.source: a phone camera roll: DCIM/Camera is one flat folder

layouts.note: DCF (JEITA CP-3461) caps a folder at 9,999 files; many bodies roll over earlier, at 999 or 2,000
RAW+JPEG of one frame share the basename; .xmp sidecars possible

bursts.source: enthusiast bursts of 5-20 frames at 10-30 fps; pre-capture and sports sequences of 50-200 frames

files.source: typical measured; MP from maker specs

files.note: medium format (100 MP) reaches about 200 MB; the embedded preview is 1616x1080 up to full size, per camera model

storage.note: phone UFS 3.1/4.0 or desktop SSD; small random reads far slower than sequential
card reader on a phone or desktop; UHS-I bus limit 104 MB/s
often capped at 35-40 MB/s by phones and USB 2.0 hubs
camera over USB: high per-file latency, no random access
online-only files download in full on open; latency is the network's
